headline: NEW FOUND GOLD GRADUATES TO TSX TODAY AS NFGC — QUEENSWAY AND HAMMERDOWN PRODUCTION PUSH BACKED BY FULL INSTITUTIONAL ACCESS
snippet: New Found Gold Corp. commenced trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on August 26, 2026 under the symbol NFGC, graduating from the TSX Venture Exchange where it traded as NFG. The uplisting opens the stock to institutional index funds and passive mandates ahead of a dual production push: the Hammerdown Gold Project in Newfoundland targets commercial gold production in H2 2026 using the Pine Cove Mill, while the flagship Queensway Gold Project — site of the high-grade Keats Zone — advances toward Phase 1 production with full funding in place.

headline: FURY GOLD DRILLS 14.41 g/t OVER 3.92m AT EAU CLAIRE — PHASE 2 INFILL ADVANCES RESOURCE UPGRADE TOWARD JAMES BAY DEVELOPMENT DECISION
snippet: Fury Gold Mines released the third batch of Phase 2 infill assay results from its Eau Claire Gold Project in the James Bay region of Quebec, highlighted by hole 26EC-125 returning 14.41 g/t Au over 3.92 metres. The 15,000–25,000-metre Phase 2 program is explicitly designed to upgrade inferred resources to indicated or measured categories ahead of a resource update; 22 holes totalling 11,423 metres have now been assayed, with additional results pending from the remaining 13 holes.

headline: BANYAN GOLD HITS 544 g/t Ag AND 5.70 g/t Au AT BRAND-NEW SEATTLE CREEK SYSTEM — GREENFIELDS DISCOVERY 25km FROM AURMAC DEPOSIT, YUKON
snippet: Banyan Gold Corp. (TSXV: BYN) announced that diamond drillhole NT-26-006 — the first hole at Seattle Creek on the 100%-owned Nitra Project in Yukon — confirmed a new high-grade gold-silver system hosted in extensional quartz veins with visible gold, bismuth sulphosalts, and arsenopyrite. The reported intercept of 5.70 g/t Au and 544 g/t Ag over 0.5m sits within the top 95m of a 600m hole that is still being assayed, and Seattle Creek is the second of eleven priority targets on Banyan's 830 sq km AurMac–Nitra land package in the Mayo Mining District.

headline: GOLIATH EXPANDS GOLDEN GATE ZONE 38% TO 1.17km² AND BONANZA TO 1.51km² — SUREBET STILL OPEN IN GOLDEN TRIANGLE, 50,000m DRILL UNDERWAY
snippet: Goliath Resources reported the latest 2026 assay batch from the Surebet Discovery on its 100%-owned Golddigger Property in the Golden Triangle, British Columbia, confirming area expansion of the Golden Gate Zone from 0.85 km² to 1.17 km² (+38%) and the Bonanza Zone from 1.27 km² to 1.51 km² (+19%). The zones remain open in multiple directions. With 52 of 98 planned holes completed totalling 31,994 metres, the fully funded 50,000m 2026 program is roughly 64% complete.

headline: ARIZONA EAGLE FINDS ZINC-SILVER VMS 200m FROM McCABE MINE — NEW SYSTEM TYPE OPENS SECOND TARGET AT TSXV:AZEM IN HISTORIC ARIZONA DISTRICT
snippet: Arizona Eagle Mining Corp. (TSXV: AZEM) reported that Phase 1 drill holes Eagle-26-05 and Eagle-26-06, drilled 200–250 metres northeast of the historic McCabe gold-silver mine in Arizona, both intersected high-grade zinc-silver VMS-type mineralization at approximately 150 metres depth. The intervals sit on strike with three past-producing silver mines recently acquired by the company, and bear strong similarities to the Iron King Mine — a former producer mined to below 1,000m depth — located approximately four kilometres along strike. A SkyTem airborne geophysical survey has been commissioned to refine Phase 2 targets.

headline: PLATINUM POSTS BEST WEEK IN 2026 AT +7.75% — WPIC 297,000oz FOURTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT AND ZIMBABWE EXPORT BAN TIGHTEN ABOVE-GROUND STOCKS
snippet: Platinum was the best-performing precious metal in the week ending August 22, rising 7.75% as the World Platinum Investment Council's revised 2026 deficit forecast of 297,000 ounces — the fourth consecutive annual shortfall — received renewed attention from traders. Above-ground inventories now cover only about four months of demand (lowest since 2014), and Zimbabwe's ban on the export of unrefined critical minerals has added further constraint to a complex where South Africa, Russia, and Zimbabwe control roughly 90% of primary supply.

headline: GDXJ A 'SCREAMING BUY' AFTER GOLD MINERS' NEAR-RECORD Q2 — SECTOR P/E COLLAPSES FROM 49.6x TO 16.5x AS EARNINGS OUTRUN STOCK PRICES
snippet: A new Investing.com analysis argues GDXJ presents a rare anomaly: unit profits at near-record levels (Q2'26 at the GDX top 25's second-best quarter ever) while the sector's trailing P/E has crashed from 49.6x after Q4 2023 to just 16.5x midweek — the lowest in at least 41 quarters and likely ever. The author contends that the miner lag versus physical gold is not a fundamental discount but a sentiment gap that historically closes violently, making GDXJ the higher-conviction vehicle heading into Q3.

headline: GOLD MID-TIERS HIT RECORD LOW 28.8% AISC-TO-GOLD RATIO IN Q2 — MARGINS NEVER BEEN FATTER BUT MARKET IS STILL PRICING IN RATE-RISK HAIRCUT
snippet: GoldSeek's quarterly analysis of gold mid-tier miners finds that Q2 2026 AISC-to-gold price ratios fell to a record low 28.8%, meaning mid-tier producers are keeping more of every gold ounce mined than at any measured point in the cycle. Despite this, mid-tier stocks remain at depressed multiples as the market reprices rate-cut optionality. The analysis concludes that for investors willing to hold through the September Fed meeting, current entry points in the mid-tiers represent the best margin-to-valuation ratio since the 2018 capitulation.

headline: SIL +35% AND SILJ +32% IN AUGUST: HOW TO PICK THE RIGHT SILVER MINER ETF — HECLA +47%, WHEATON +44%, FIRST MAJESTIC +42% AS METAL SURGES
snippet: With SIL (Global X Silver Miners) and SILJ (ETFMG Prime Junior Silver Miners) both surging 35% and 32% respectively in August on the back of silver's 20% run to $70/oz, TipRanks breaks down which ETF structure offers better risk-adjusted exposure. Individual standouts: Hecla Mining +47% (largest pure-play silver producer in the US), Wheaton Precious Metals +44%, First Majestic Silver and Coeur Mining both +42%. The piece highlights that junior ETFs carry higher beta but also higher single-stock risk heading into the September Fed decision.

headline: TERBIUM AT $3,600-5,000/kg OUTSIDE CHINA VS $989 DOMESTIC — RARE EARTH PRICE DIVIDE WIDENS AS WESTERN SUPPLY CHAINS APPROACH STRESS TEST
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges analysis of the China–Western price divide finds the gap in heavy rare earths is now structurally entrenched: terbium, a critical input for permanent magnets in EVs and wind turbines, commands $3,600–5,000/kg in stressed Western markets versus approximately $989/kg in China, while dysprosium carries similarly outsized premiums. NdPr oxide in China stands at ¥711–731/kg ($106–109) versus the US Department of Defense's contracted floor of $110/kg for MP Materials and disclosed floors around $2,050/kg for terbium in the Serra Verde–USA Rare Earth arrangement — illustrating why Western rare earth project economics look very different from Chinese benchmarks.
